subject: c12-chem
note: Official CBSE Class XII Chemistry theory paper: 70 marks. The 2026-27 course structure assigns marks directly to the ten listed units; practical is separate.
mistakes: Solutions: confusing molarity and molality or using temperature-dependent concentration units in a temperature-sensitive context.
Solutions: applying colligative-property relations without checking the van't Hoff factor or abnormal-molar-mass condition.
Electrochemistry: reversing anode/cathode or oxidation/reduction signs when moving between galvanic and electrolytic cells.
Electrochemistry: using the Nernst equation with an incorrect reaction quotient or inconsistent logarithm convention.
Chemical Kinetics: mixing zero-order and first-order integrated equations and half-life relations.
Chemical Kinetics: confusing rate constant units with reaction rate units.
d- and f-Block: memorising trends without distinguishing general transition-metal behaviour from specific exceptions and compounds.
Coordination Compounds: losing track of ligand names, coordination number, oxidation state, geometry and isomerism while naming a complex.
Organic Chemistry: writing a reaction without checking the reagent, condition, substrate class and major product.
Amines: confusing basicity trends and chemical properties, or mixing diazotisation and coupling conditions.
Biomolecules: memorising classifications without connecting monomers, linkages, functions and examples.
order: Do Solutions, Electrochemistry and Chemical Kinetics first; practise their numerical patterns immediately after learning each concept.
Study d- and f-Block with a compact trend/compound sheet and revise it repeatedly rather than cramming once.
Complete Coordination Compounds next, especially terminology, nomenclature, isomerism and bonding.
Study the organic sequence in order: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes → Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers → Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids → Amines.
Finish Biomolecules with linked tables for carbohydrates, proteins, enzymes, vitamins, nucleic acids and hormones.
After the first complete pass, practise mixed conversion/reaction questions and numerical questions together.
Use the official sample paper and marking scheme to check answer style and coverage.
